\section{Result and scope}\label{result-and-scope}

The original arithmetic source is recovered exactly by the complete
family of twisted circle periodizations. The new calculation retains
what happens when minimization over the original theta relations is
performed in that family. There is a positive, explicitly calculated
difference between the original quotient metric and the average of the
fibre quotient metrics. It is the norm of a family of original
relations, not an unspecified error.

If every phase-source Gram lies between \((1-\eta)M\) and \((1+\eta)M\),
where \(M\) is their exact mean and \(0\leq\eta<1\), the calculated
comparison is

\[
 (1-\eta^2)G\preceq \overline G\preceq G,
 \qquad
 G-\overline G
 =\int (C-C_\theta)^*M_\theta(C-C_\theta)\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}.
 \tag{H1}
\]

Here \(C\) and \(C_\theta\) are minimum-norm sections of the
\textbf{same} original polynomial quotient. Every difference
\(C-C_\theta\) has its actual theta primitive. The factor \(\eta^2\) is
sharp for the stated matrix hypotheses. This is an application of
positive-matrix variational methods, not a priority claim for operator
concavity.

The family is joined to finite cyclic covers, the new
residue-constituent coefficient, and the original endpoint-volume
criterion. All these constructions remain over the marked split base. No
finite-field weight theorem is applied to a Hilbert circle quotient. No
uniform arithmetic upper bound contradicting the inherited quartet
threshold is proved in this note.

\section{1. Fixed inputs, maps, and the marked split
base}\label{fixed-inputs-maps-and-the-marked-split-base}

The owner's scalar object, its support observation, and its arithmetic
observation are retained:

\[
 G(R)=\{\tau\}\sqcup R^\bullet,\quad e_R=0_R^\bullet,\qquad
 p_R(\tau)=0,\quad p_R(r^\bullet)=r,\qquad
 b_R(\tau)=0_{\mathbb B},\quad b_R(r^\bullet)=1_{\mathbb B}.
 \tag{H2}
\]

The map \((p_R,b_R)\) is injective. The arithmetic coefficient square is

\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
G(\mathbb Z)&\xrightarrow{G(\jmath)}&G(\mathbb C)\\
p_{\mathbb Z}\downarrow&&\downarrow p_{\mathbb C}\\
\mathbb Z&\xrightarrow{\jmath}&\mathbb C.
\end{array}
\tag{H3}
\]

The target of \(p_{\mathbb Z}\) is infinite. The pointed-monoid base has
structure map \(\{\tau_0,1\}\to U_\times G(R)\), taking \(\tau_0\) to
\(\tau\) and \(1\) to \(1^\bullet\). Direct image to its point retains
the coefficient object; it is not replaced by its Boolean localization.

On a fixed original support label \(\ell\), a coefficient-linear map
\(f\) lifts by

\[
 (\ell,v)\longmapsto(\ell,fv),\qquad \tau\longmapsto\tau.
 \tag{H4}
\]

For a relation submodule \(B_\ell\), the quotient is
\((\ell,v)\mapsto(\ell,[v])\). Its equality criterion is
\(v-v'\in B_\ell\). Thus \(f(v)=0\) gives the receiving fibre zero, not
external absence. Every map constructed below has this lift. Products of
phase fibres use the original product support diagram; on a common label
the scalar Fourier matrices give linear equivalences. For unequal
labels, sums first use the stated joins and transports. No injectivity
of arbitrary support transports is assumed.

Retain the original theta data

\[
 V=\{\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)_{\mathrm{ev}}:\phi(0)=0,\ \int\phi=0\},
 \quad\Theta\phi(x)=2\sum_{n\geq1}\phi(nx),\quad
 Q=\mathscr B/\Theta V,\quad D=-x\partial_x,\quad g=2\xi.
 \tag{H5}
\]

The prior full-jet analytic construction supplies \(F_h\in\mathscr B\)
with \(\mathcal MF_h=g/h\), for a selected finite packet \(h\) with
every selected order complete. The present finite arithmetic module is

\[
 E=\mathbb C[S]/(\chi_{h,k}),\quad q=\deg\chi_{h,k}>0,\quad A=M_S,
 \qquad S=s_1+\cdots+s_k.
 \tag{H6}
\]

Use its same source map and full inclusion:

\[
 \mathcal V P=P(D_1+\cdots+D_k)F_h^{\otimes k},\qquad
 J^{(k)}\mathcal V=\eta\pi_\chi,
 \qquad q^{(k)}\mathcal V=\sigma_h^{\otimes k}\eta\pi_\chi,
 \tag{H7}
\]

\[
 \eta[P]=\upsilon_h^{\otimes k}P(A_k)1,
 \qquad \upsilon_h=j_h(g/h).
 \tag{H8}
\]

The unit in (H8), every nilpotent jet, and \(g=2\xi\) stay in these
equations. For \(N\geq q-1\), let \(P_N=\mathbb C[S]_{\leq N}\),
\(J_N=\pi_\chi|_{P_N}\), and \(B_N=\ker J_N=\chi P_{N-q}\), where
\(P_{-1}=0\). Fix their coefficient bases. A matrix denoted \(B\) below
is the injective coefficient matrix for multiplication by this literal
\(\chi\); it is not a replacement of a higher contracted relation ideal
by a power of \(\chi\).

The new source corrections are incorporated as follows. The supplied
primary-source correction resolves the reference at Weil II 3.7.4 as
Roman I.8.11 in Weil I. The strict bound in 3.2.10, the square in
3.2.13, and the lisse/mixed hypotheses in 1.8.12 remain. The supplied
translation note keeps its scalar \(\exp((-\Phi(-a)-ta)/u)\); the marked
arithmetic fibre remains \(a=0\). The supplied residue note's exact
rank-one and curvature identities are inherited inputs in Section 8, not
discoveries of this continuation.

\section{2. All circle holonomies recover the full
source}\label{all-circle-holonomies-recover-the-full-source}

Retain the predecessor's exact logarithmic coordinates

\[
 r=\log x_k,\quad z_i=\log x_i-\log x_k\ (i<k),\qquad
 (\mathcal U_k F)(r,z)=e^{(kr+\sum z_i)/2}
 F(e^{r+z_1},\ldots,e^{r+z_{k-1}},e^r).
 \tag{H9}
\]

Their logarithmic Jacobian is one. With
\(\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^{k-1},dz)\), this is an isometry into
\(L^2(\mathbb R,dr;\mathcal K)\), and

\[
 \mathcal U_kD^{(k)}=(-\partial_r+k/2)\mathcal U_k.
 \tag{H10}
\]

No relative variable is integrated out of the vector-valued source.
Integrals in this note are defined inside each specified coefficient
fibre, then lifted by (H4); no unconstructed integration operation on
arbitrary mixed-support carriers is assumed. For \(L>0\) and
\(0\leq\theta<2\pi\), define

\[
 (\mathcal Z_{L,\theta}\psi)(r)=
 \sum_{a\in\mathbb Z}e^{ia\theta}\psi(r+aL),\quad0\leq r<L.
 \tag{H11}
\]

The original finite sources have sufficient weighted Schwartz bounds to
differentiate and sum this expression on compact sets. It extends to the
Hilbert-space transform by density. Its boundary and Fourier equations
are

\[
 \mathcal Z_{L,\theta}\psi(r+L)=e^{-i\theta}\mathcal Z_{L,\theta}\psi(r),
 \qquad
 \widehat{\mathcal Z_{L,\theta}\psi}(n)
 =L^{-1/2}\widehat\psi((2\pi n+\theta)/L),
 \tag{H12}
\]

where \(\widehat\psi(u)=\int\psi(r)e^{iur}dr\), and the target basis is
\(L^{-1/2}e^{-i(2\pi n+\theta)r/L}\). To check the factor, substitute
\(y=r+aL\) in the coefficient integral. The two phase factors give
\(e^{ia\theta}e^{-ia(2\pi n+\theta)}=1\).

\textbf{Exact isometry and inverse.} The full transform is

\[
 \mathcal Z_L:L^2(\mathbb R;\mathcal K)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \int_{[0,2\pi)}^{\oplus}L^2([0,L];\mathcal K)\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}.
 \tag{H13}
\]

For \(0\leq r<L\) and \(a\in\mathbb Z\), its inverse is

\[
 \psi(r+aL)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}
 e^{-ia\theta}(\mathcal Z_L\psi)(r,\theta)\,d\theta.
 \tag{H14}
\]

For each \(r\), these are precisely the Fourier-series map and inverse
on the sequence \((\psi(r+aL))_a\). Parseval followed by integration in
\(r\) proves (H13). The measure \(d\theta/(2\pi)\) is the actual Fourier
inversion measure; no arithmetic mass has been assigned the value one.

For the fixed source-column map \(\Psi_N=\mathcal U_k\mathcal V|_{P_N}\)
put

\[
 M_N(\theta)=(\mathcal Z_{L,\theta}\Psi_N)^*(\mathcal Z_{L,\theta}\Psi_N),
 \qquad M_N=\Psi_N^*\Psi_N.
 \tag{H15}
\]

Then, exactly,

\[
 \int_0^{2\pi}M_N(\theta)\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}=M_N.
 \tag{H16}
\]

The original norm is \(\int |P(k/2+iu)|^2m_{h,k}(u)du\), where
\(m_{h,k}=w_h^{*k}\) and \(w_h=|(g/h)(1/2+iu)|^2/(2\pi)\). Partial
Plancherel therefore gives

\[
 M_N(\theta)_{ab}=
 \frac{2\pi}{L}\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}
 m_{h,k}((2\pi n+\theta)/L)
 \overline{P_a(k/2+i(2\pi n+\theta)/L)}
 P_b(k/2+i(2\pi n+\theta)/L).
 \tag{H17}
\]

For \(k\geq2\) all these scalar weights are positive. Infinitely many
distinct sample points then imply positive definiteness on every finite
polynomial source. The uniform quantitative statements below instead use
the displayed relative source bound, which by itself implies positive
definiteness, including other admitted sources.

At \(\theta=0,n=0\), retain the term
\(L^{-1}\widehat\Psi_N(0)^*\widehat\Psi_N(0)\). It is not discarded in
(H15)--(H17). The phase variable is a character of the translation
lattice. It is not the coefficient translation \(a\) of the exponential
note: \(\chi\), \(A\), \(\eta\), and \(g\) are fixed throughout
(H11)--(H17).

\section{3. Every finite cyclic cover is an exact character
decomposition}\label{every-finite-cyclic-cover-is-an-exact-character-decomposition}

Let \(m\geq1\) and \(\theta_j=2\pi j/m\). For a function \(f\) on the
circle of length \(mL\), define

\[
 Q_jf(r)=\frac1m\sum_{a=0}^{m-1}e^{ia\theta_j}f(r+aL).
 \tag{H18}
\]

Finite character sums prove \(Q_jQ_l=\delta_{jl}Q_j\), \(\sum_jQ_j=I\),
and \(Q_jf(r+L)=e^{-i\theta_j}Q_jf(r)\). The actual unitary map and
inverse are

\[
 f\longmapsto(\sqrt m\,Q_jf|_{[0,L]})_{j=0}^{m-1},
 \qquad
 f(r+aL)=\frac1{\sqrt m}\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e^{-ia\theta_j}g_j(r).
 \tag{H19}
\]

The norm follows either by the finite Fourier identity or orthogonality
of the \(Q_j\) on the long circle. Applied to the same original source,

\[
 Q_j\mathcal Z_{mL,0}\psi=\frac1m\mathcal Z_{L,\theta_j}\psi,
 \qquad
 M_N(mL,0)=\frac1m\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}M_N(L,\theta_j).
 \tag{H20}
\]

The second equation is exact at every finite degree; the individual
masses are not reset. For a general phase \(\theta\), the compatible
refinement is

\[
 M_N(L,\theta)=\frac1n\sum_{a=0}^{n-1}
 M_N(L/n,(\theta+2\pi a)/n).
 \tag{H21}
\]

It follows equally by partitioning the sampled frequency lattice into
congruence classes. Repeated refinements compose because these are
literal partitions of the same lattice.

\subsection{The finite locally free coefficient
cover}\label{the-finite-locally-free-coefficient-cover}

Here is the algebraic cover that gives the finite characters, rather
than an identification with an arithmetic Frobenius. Let

\[
 A_{\mathrm{cov}}=\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}],\quad
 B_{\mathrm{cov}}=\mathbb C[w,w^{-1}],\quad z\longmapsto w^m.
 \tag{H22}
\]

The pushforward coefficient module is free with its full basis
\(1,w,\ldots,w^{m-1}\). Division of an integer exponent by \(m\) proves
this also for negative powers. For \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/m}\), the deck
action is \(\gamma_a(w)=\zeta^{-a}w\). The projector
\(m^{-1}\sum_a\zeta^{ja}\gamma_a\) has image \(A_{\mathrm{cov}}w^j\);
multiplication of those summands retains the extra factor \(z\) when
indices cross \(m\).

The derivative \(mw^{m-1}\) is invertible. This proves this particular
cover is finite étale, hence finite locally free. EGA I, 1.6.3 and 9.2,
and EGA II, 6.1 describe the affine direct-image and finite-morphism
setting; here the module and projectors are written explicitly. The
base-change map is

\[
 B_{\mathrm{cov}}\otimes_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}A'
 \xrightarrow{\sim} A'[w,w^{-1}]/(w^m-z'),
 \qquad b\otimes a'\longmapsto a'b(w).
 \tag{H23}
\]

The circle restriction is \(w=e^{-2\pi ir/(mL)}\), \(z=e^{-2\pi ir/L}\)
and yields (H18). Applying \(G\) to the ring map in (H22) commutes with
(H3), and fixes \(\tau\) and \(e\). Character projectors act linearly on
the coefficient fibres. A coefficient projected to zero is a represented
fibre zero. These idempotent endomorphisms are not relabelled as the
supported-zero scalar \(e\).

This is a use of the finite-cover and same-image architecture, not a
proof of arithmetic weight bounds from finite étaleness. No six-functor
theorem for the split semiring category is asserted.

\section{4. Common arithmetic representatives and the exact descent
cost}\label{common-arithmetic-representatives-and-the-exact-descent-cost}

Suppress \(N\) for this section. Let \(J:P_N\to E\) be the original
surjection, let \(B:\mathbb C^r\hookrightarrow P_N\) be the coefficient
matrix of \(\chi P_{N-q}\), and retain \(M=\int M_\theta\). For each
phase and the common source, define

\[
 G=(JM^{-1}J^*)^{-1},\quad C=M^{-1}J^*G,
 \qquad
 G_\theta=(JM_\theta^{-1}J^*)^{-1},\quad
 C_\theta=M_\theta^{-1}J^*G_\theta.
 \tag{H24}
\]

These formulas hold at \(N=q-1\) too: the relation column space then has
dimension zero and the corresponding correction is zero. The
empty-packet coefficient module has empty Gram determinant one and is
handled separately; it does not erase the nonzero analytic seed.

The defining equations are

\[
 JC=JC_\theta=I_E,\quad B^*MC=0,\quad B^*M_\theta C_\theta=0.
 \tag{H25}
\]

Consequently there is a unique coefficient map
\(X_\theta:E\to\mathbb C^r\) with

\[
 C-C_\theta=BX_\theta,\qquad
 X_\theta=(B^*M_\theta B)^{-1}B^*M_\theta C.
 \tag{H26}
\]

The last formula follows by applying \(B^*M_\theta\) to the first. Thus
every discrepancy is in the original relation submodule, and monic
division followed by the existing tensor theta primitive realizes it in
the original cochain complex.

Set

\[
 \overline G=\int G_\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi},\qquad
 \mathscr D=\int X_\theta^*(B^*M_\theta B)X_\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}.
 \tag{H27}
\]

The fundamental identity is

\[
 \boxed{G=\overline G+\mathscr D.}
 \tag{H28}
\]

\textbf{Proof.} Write \(C=C_\theta+BX_\theta\) and expand
\(C^*M_\theta C\). Both cross terms vanish by (H25), leaving
\(G_\theta+X_\theta^*B^*M_\theta BX_\theta\). Integrating gives
\(C^*MC=G\). Every integrand is positive semidefinite. Uniform source
bounds justify the finite-dimensional integrals and their inverses; for
continuous positive definite matrices on the compact phase circle these
bounds also exist without a specified value.

Equation (H28) is the exact difference between first taking the
common-source quotient and first minimizing separately in each phase. It
replaces a proposed interchange of those operations with a calculated
relation norm.

\subsection{The cochain comparison and its full contractible
complement}\label{the-cochain-comparison-and-its-full-contractible-complement}

For \(m\) phases put

\[
 \mathcal P^{\mathrm{eq}}_{N,m}
 =\{(P_j)\in P_N^m:JP_j\text{ is independent of }j\}.
 \tag{H29}
\]

There are actual complexes in degrees \(0,1\),

\[
 [B_N\hookrightarrow P_N]
 \xrightarrow{\Delta_m}
 [B_N^m\hookrightarrow\mathcal P^{\mathrm{eq}}_{N,m}],
 \tag{H30}
\]

where \(\Delta_m\) repeats every coefficient. The reverse cochain map is
\(\operatorname{av}_m(P_j)=m^{-1}\sum_jP_j\) in each degree. It
satisfies \(\operatorname{av}_m\Delta_m=I\). The complement is

\[
 \mathcal B_{N,m}^{0}
 =\{(b_j)\in B_N^m:\sum_jb_j=0\},\qquad
 [\mathcal B_{N,m}^{0}\xrightarrow{I}\mathcal B_{N,m}^{0}].
 \tag{H31}
\]

The inverse coefficient coordinates are
\(P_j\mapsto(\overline P,(P_j-\overline P)_j)\) and
\((P,(b_j))\mapsto(P+b_j)_j\). Since all jets agree, each difference
lies in \(B_N\). They prove the asserted direct-sum decomposition of
complexes, and the identity is the explicit contraction on the
complement. Both complexes have the same degree-one \(E\), with original
arithmetic inclusion \(\eta\). In original arithmetic degree \(k\) the
complement has degrees \(k-1,k\), so an endomorphism preserving this
decomposition has its two complement traces with opposite cohomological
signs.

The maps are strict for the stated polynomial filtration: repeating a
polynomial does not lower its degree, and averaging a degree-\(N\) tuple
remains degree at most \(N\). More explicitly,
\(\Delta_m(P_N)=\operatorname{im}\Delta_m\cap P_N^m\), and averaging the
equal-jet tuples at degree \(N\) is onto \(P_N\). The multiplication map
\(M_S:P_N\to P_{N+1}\) commutes with both operations; its quotient is
the original \(A\). At a fixed cutoff it is a degree-raising map, not a
presumed endomorphism of \(P_N\).

The complement's cohomology is zero, but its source norm is present in
(H27)--(H28). Its contraction is not asserted isometric. Split
reconstruction retains its represented vectors, the corresponding
supported-zero maps, and external absence. Thus the exactness on the
common image does not supply a missing norm estimate by itself.

\section{5. Sharp quadratic control of the descent
cost}\label{sharp-quadratic-control-of-the-descent-cost}

\textbf{Theorem.} Let \(M_\theta\succ0\) be the specified source
matrices with mean \(M\), and suppose

\[
 (1-\eta)M\preceq M_\theta\preceq(1+\eta)M,
 \qquad 0\leq\eta<1.
 \tag{H32}
\]

Then for the original \(J\) and (H24),

\[
 \boxed{(1-\eta^2)G\preceq\overline G\preceq G,
 \qquad 0\preceq\mathscr D\preceq\eta^2G.}
 \tag{H33}
\]

\textbf{Proof of the upper inequality.} It is (H28).

\textbf{Proof of the lower inequality.} For \(x\in[1-\eta,1+\eta]\), the
complete scalar identity is

\[
 \frac{2-x}{1-\eta^2}-\frac1x
 =\frac{\eta^2-(x-1)^2}{x(1-\eta^2)}\geq0.
 \tag{H34}
\]

The endomorphism \(X_\theta=M^{-1}M_\theta\) is positive self-adjoint in
the retained \(M\)-metric and has that spectral interval. Applying (H34)
to this finite operator and composing with the displayed metric-dual map
\(M^{-1}\) proves

\[
 M_\theta^{-1}\preceq
 \frac{2M^{-1}-M^{-1}M_\theta M^{-1}}{1-\eta^2}.
 \tag{H35}
\]

Averaging retains \(\int M_\theta=M\) and gives

\[
 \overline K:=\int JM_\theta^{-1}J^*\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}
 \preceq (1-\eta^2)^{-1}K,\qquad K=JM^{-1}J^*=G^{-1}.
 \tag{H36}
\]

For each phase the block matrix

\[
 \begin{pmatrix}K_\theta&I_E\\I_E&G_\theta\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
 \tag{H37}
\]

is positive: its quadratic form is
\((x+G_\theta y)^*K_\theta(x+G_\theta y)\). Averaging and taking the
Schur complement gives \(\overline G\succeq\overline K^{-1}\). Inverting
(H36) proves the lower inequality of (H33). This proof does not change
the original metric, discard the mean condition, or choose a new section
to fit a desired form.

More generally, \(aM\preceq M_\theta\preceq bM\), \(0<a\leq1\leq b\),
gives

\[
 \overline G\succeq\frac{ab}{a+b-1}G,
 \qquad
 G-\overline G\preceq
 \frac{(1-a)(b-1)}{a+b-1}G.
 \tag{H38}
\]

The inverse chord is \(x^{-1}\leq(a+b-x)/(ab)\) on \([a,b]\); the same
proof applies.

These are variational positive-operator calculations related to the
classical shorted-operator construction. The contribution here is the
exact supported source, common jet map, family of theta primitives, and
phase recovery to which they are applied.

\subsection{The arithmetic hypothesis is supplied by the existing
correlation
bound}\label{the-arithmetic-hypothesis-is-supplied-by-the-existing-correlation-bound}

For \(a>0\), retain the two actual weighted Grams

\[
 M_{a,\pm}=(e^{\pm ar}\Psi_N)^*(e^{\pm ar}\Psi_N),\qquad
 \kappa_{a,N}=
 \sup_{v\ne0}\frac{v^*(M_{a,+}+M_{a,-})v}{v^*Mv}.
 \tag{H39}
\]

Their original coordinate factors are \(x_k^{\pm2a}\). With
\(\mathcal C(s)=\int\Psi_N(r)^*\Psi_N(r+s)dr\), unfolding gives

\[
 M_N(\theta)=\sum_{b\in\mathbb Z}e^{ib\theta}\mathcal C(bL).
 \tag{H40}
\]

Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz bounds each quadratic correlation by
\(e^{-a|s|}\sqrt{(v^*M_{a,+}v)(v^*M_{a,-}v)}\). Summing both signs
proves, uniformly in phase,

\[
 -\delta_LM\preceq M_N(\theta)-M\preceq\delta_LM,
 \qquad \delta_L=\frac{\kappa_{a,N}}{e^{aL}-1}.
 \tag{H41}
\]

Thus any specified \(L\) with \(\delta_L<1\) supplies (H32). The passage
from source error to the averaged quotient error is now quadratic:
\(\mathscr D\preceq\delta_L^2G\). Growth of \(\kappa_{a,N}\) with the
arithmetic packet is not bounded by (H41).

\section{6. Endpoints and a genuinely finite phase
construction}\label{endpoints-and-a-genuinely-finite-phase-construction}

Apply the uniform phase bound to one finite source containing all four
endpoint spaces, for example the original degree \(2q+2\) source.
Restriction gives the same \(\eta\) on every smaller source. Write
\(V_N=\det G_N\) and \(\overline V_N=\det\overline G_N\).

Equation (H33) proves

\[
 q\log(1-\eta^2)\leq
 \log\overline V_N-\log V_N\leq0.
 \tag{H42}
\]

For \(\mathcal B=\log(V_{q-1}V_q/(V_{2q-1}V_{2q}))\) and its
averaged-metric analogue \(\overline{\mathcal B}\),

\[
 \boxed{|\overline{\mathcal B}-\mathcal B|
 \leq2q\log\frac1{1-\eta^2}.}
 \tag{H43}
\]

The complete equality remains available:

\[
 V_N=\overline V_N\det(I+\overline G_N^{-1}\mathscr D_N).
 \tag{H44}
\]

The endomorphism \(\overline G_N^{-1}\mathscr D_N\) is positive
self-adjoint for \(\overline G_N\). Both its source map and its
determinant contribution are specified. In particular, averaging the
quotient metrics without the correction in (H44) is not an asserted
exact reconstruction.

At \(m\) equally spaced phases define

\[
 M^{(m)}=\frac1m\sum_jM(L,\theta_j)=M(mL,0),\quad
 G^{(m)}=(J(M^{(m)})^{-1}J^*)^{-1},\quad
 \overline G^{(m)}=\frac1m\sum_jG(L,\theta_j).
 \tag{H45}
\]

Every formula (H24)--(H28) holds exactly with this finite mean and its
actual canonical section. To compare this finite construction with the
original \(M\), put

\[
 \delta_m=\frac{\kappa_{a,N}}{e^{amL}-1},\qquad
 \nu_m=\frac{\delta_L+\delta_m}{1-\delta_m}.
 \tag{H46}
\]

For \(\delta_m<1\) and \(\nu_m<1\), triangle inequalities relative to
\(M\) and \(M^{(m)}\) give

\[
 (1-\nu_m)M^{(m)}\preceq M(L,\theta_j)
 \preceq(1+\nu_m)M^{(m)}.
 \tag{H47}
\]

The theorem and the original quotient transport then prove

\[
 \boxed{
 (1-\nu_m^2)(1-\delta_m)G
 \preceq\overline G^{(m)}\preceq(1+\delta_m)G.}
 \tag{H48}
\]

Consequently the finite-phase four-volume error is at most

\[
 2q\log\frac{1+\delta_m}{(1-\delta_m)(1-\nu_m^2)}.
 \tag{H49}
\]

For fixed sufficiently large \(L\), \(\delta_m\) tends to zero
exponentially with the number of phases. The remaining comparison cost
tends to the proved quadratic bound, rather than to an unproved zero.

\subsection{Exponentially convergent quadrature for the quotient
itself}\label{exponentially-convergent-quadrature-for-the-quotient-itself}

The exact finite-cover identity controls the source mean. There is also
a direct, quantitative convergence estimate for the mean of the quotient
metrics, with the original matrix inversions included.

Let \(\kappa_\pm\) be the individual largest generalized eigenvalues of
\((M_{a,\pm},M)\). Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz on two distinct vectors
proves

\[
 \|M^{-1}\mathcal C(nL)\|_M
 \leq\sqrt{\kappa_+\kappa_-}\,e^{-a|n|L}.
 \tag{H49a}
\]

Here \(\|\cdot\|_M\) is the operator norm in the original source metric.
Choose \(s>0\) with \(s<aL\) and retain

\[
 d_s=\frac{2\sqrt{\kappa_+\kappa_-}}{e^{aL-s}-1}<1.
 \tag{H49b}
\]

The correlation series defines a holomorphic matrix \(\widetilde M(z)\)
on \(|\Im z|<aL\), agreeing with \(M_\theta\) on the real axis, and
\(\|M^{-1}(\widetilde M(z)-M)\|_M\leq d_s\) on \(|\Im z|\leq s\). This
is a holomorphic extension of the real-axis Gram coefficients. It is not
defined by conjugating the complex parameter in a new Gram formula.

Retain the common section \(C\) and original relation columns \(B\) from

\subsection{The finite locally free coefficient
cover}\label{the-finite-locally-free-coefficient-cover}

Here is the algebraic cover that gives the finite characters, rather
than an identification with an arithmetic Frobenius. Let

\[
 A_{\mathrm{cov}}=\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}],\quad
 B_{\mathrm{cov}}=\mathbb C[w,w^{-1}],\quad z\longmapsto w^m.
 \tag{H22}
\]

The pushforward coefficient module is free with its full basis
\(1,w,\ldots,w^{m-1}\). Division of an integer exponent by \(m\) proves
this also for negative powers. For \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/m}\), the deck
action is \(\gamma_a(w)=\zeta^{-a}w\). The projector
\(m^{-1}\sum_a\zeta^{ja}\gamma_a\) has image \(A_{\mathrm{cov}}w^j\);
multiplication of those summands retains the extra factor \(z\) when
indices cross \(m\).

The derivative \(mw^{m-1}\) is invertible. This proves this particular
cover is finite étale, hence finite locally free. EGA I, 1.6.3 and 9.2,
and EGA II, 6.1 describe the affine direct-image and finite-morphism
setting; here the module and projectors are written explicitly. The
base-change map is

\[
 B_{\mathrm{cov}}\otimes_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}A'
 \xrightarrow{\sim} A'[w,w^{-1}]/(w^m-z'),
 \qquad b\otimes a'\longmapsto a'b(w).
 \tag{H23}
\]

The circle restriction is \(w=e^{-2\pi ir/(mL)}\), \(z=e^{-2\pi ir/L}\)
and yields (H18). Applying \(G\) to the ring map in (H22) commutes with
(H3), and fixes \(\tau\) and \(e\). Character projectors act linearly on
the coefficient fibres. A coefficient projected to zero is a represented
fibre zero. These idempotent endomorphisms are not relabelled as the
supported-zero scalar \(e\).

This is a use of the finite-cover and same-image architecture, not a
proof of arithmetic weight bounds from finite étaleness. No six-functor
theorem for the split semiring category is asserted.

\section{4. Common arithmetic representatives and the exact descent

surjection, let \(B:\mathbb C^r\hookrightarrow P_N\) be the coefficient
matrix of \(\chi P_{N-q}\), and retain \(M=\int M_\theta\). For each
phase and the common source, define

\[
 G=(JM^{-1}J^*)^{-1},\quad C=M^{-1}J^*G,
 \qquad

 C_\theta=M_\theta^{-1}J^*G_\theta.
 \tag{H24}
\]

These formulas hold at \(N=q-1\) too: the relation column space then has
dimension zero and the corresponding correction is zero. The
empty-packet coefficient module has empty Gram determinant one and is
handled separately; it does not erase the nonzero analytic seed.

The defining equations are

\[
 JC=JC_\theta=I_E,\quad B^*MC=0,\quad B^*M_\theta C_\theta=0.
 \tag{H25}
\]

Consequently there is a unique coefficient map
\(X_\theta:E\to\mathbb C^r\) with

\[
 C-C_\theta=BX_\theta,\qquad
 X_\theta=(B^*M_\theta B)^{-1}B^*M_\theta C.
 \tag{H26}
\]

The last formula follows by applying \(B^*M_\theta\) to the first. Thus
every discrepancy is in the original relation submodule, and monic
division followed by the existing tensor theta primitive realizes it in
the original cochain complex.

\[
 \overline G=\int G_\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi},\qquad
 \mathscr D=\int X_\theta^*(B^*M_\theta B)X_\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}.
 \tag{H27}
\]

The fundamental identity is

\[
 \boxed{G=\overline G+\mathscr D.}
 \tag{H28}
\]

\textbf{Proof.} Write \(C=C_\theta+BX_\theta\) and expand
\(C^*M_\theta C\). Both cross terms vanish by (H25), leaving
\(G_\theta+X_\theta^*B^*M_\theta BX_\theta\). Integrating gives
\(C^*MC=G\). Every integrand is positive semidefinite. Uniform source
bounds justify the finite-dimensional integrals and their inverses; for
continuous positive definite matrices on the compact phase circle these
bounds also exist without a specified value.

Equation (H28) is the exact difference between first taking the
common-source quotient and first minimizing separately in each phase. It
replaces a proposed interchange of those operations with a calculated

\subsection{The cochain comparison and its full contractible
complement}\label{the-cochain-comparison-and-its-full-contractible-complement}

 =\{(P_j)\in P_N^m:JP_j\text{ is independent of }j\}.
 \tag{H29}

\(\operatorname{av}_m(P_j)=m^{-1}\sum_jP_j\) in each degree. It
satisfies \(\operatorname{av}_m\Delta_m=I\). The complement is

\[

 \tag{H31}
\]

\(P_j\mapsto(\overline P,(P_j-\overline P)_j)\) and
\((P,(b_j))\mapsto(P+b_j)_j\). Since all jets agree, each difference
lies in \(B_N\). They prove the asserted direct-sum decomposition of

\(\Delta_m(P_N)=\operatorname{im}\Delta_m\cap P_N^m\), and averaging the

\(M_S:P_N\to P_{N+1}\) commutes with both operations; its quotient is

\section{5. Sharp quadratic control of the descent
cost}\label{sharp-quadratic-control-of-the-descent-cost}

\textbf{Theorem.} Let \(M_\theta\succ0\) be the specified source
matrices with mean \(M\), and suppose

\[
 (1-\eta)M\preceq M_\theta\preceq(1+\eta)M,
 \qquad 0\leq\eta<1.
 \tag{H32}
\]

Then for the original \(J\) and (H24),

\[
 \boxed{(1-\eta^2)G\preceq\overline G\preceq G,
 \qquad 0\preceq\mathscr D\preceq\eta^2G.}
 \tag{H33}
\]

\textbf{Proof of the upper inequality.} It is (H28).

\textbf{Proof of the lower inequality.} For \(x\in[1-\eta,1+\eta]\), the
complete scalar identity is

\[
 \frac{2-x}{1-\eta^2}-\frac1x
 =\frac{\eta^2-(x-1)^2}{x(1-\eta^2)}\geq0.
 \tag{H34}
\]

The endomorphism \(X_\theta=M^{-1}M_\theta\) is positive self-adjoint in
the retained \(M\)-metric and has that spectral interval. Applying (H34)
to this finite operator and composing with the displayed metric-dual map
\(M^{-1}\) proves

\[
 M_\theta^{-1}\preceq
 \frac{2M^{-1}-M^{-1}M_\theta M^{-1}}{1-\eta^2}.
 \tag{H35}
\]

Averaging retains \(\int M_\theta=M\) and gives

\[
 \overline K:=\int JM_\theta^{-1}J^*\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}
 \preceq (1-\eta^2)^{-1}K,\qquad K=JM^{-1}J^*=G^{-1}.
 \tag{H36}
\]

For each phase the block matrix

\[
 \begin{pmatrix}K_\theta&I_E\\I_E&G_\theta\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
 \tag{H37}
\]

is positive: its quadratic form is
\((x+G_\theta y)^*K_\theta(x+G_\theta y)\). Averaging and taking the
Schur complement gives \(\overline G\succeq\overline K^{-1}\). Inverting
(H36) proves the lower inequality of (H33). This proof does not change
the original metric, discard the mean condition, or choose a new section
to fit a desired form.

More generally, \(aM\preceq M_\theta\preceq bM\), \(0<a\leq1\leq b\),
gives

\[
 \overline G\succeq\frac{ab}{a+b-1}G,
 \qquad
 G-\overline G\preceq
 \frac{(1-a)(b-1)}{a+b-1}G.
 \tag{H38}
\]

The inverse chord is \(x^{-1}\leq(a+b-x)/(ab)\) on \([a,b]\); the same
proof applies.

These are variational positive-operator calculations related to the
classical shorted-operator construction. The contribution here is the
exact supported source, common jet map, family of theta primitives, and
phase recovery to which they are applied.

\[
 \mathcal C_N=[B_N\hookrightarrow P_N],\qquad
 \mathscr C_N=[\mathscr B\hookrightarrow\mathscr P^{\rm eq}].
 \tag{HCD4}

 \|\Delta v\|_{\mathscr P}^2

\[
 \|\av P\|_M^2

 \begin{gathered}
 \mathscr C_N\simeq

lies in $B_N$ and equals $BX_\theta$; multiplication by

 \boxed{
 \begin{aligned}
 G-\overline G=\mathscr D
 &=\int(C-C_\theta)^*M_\theta(C-C_\theta)\,d\mu\\
 &=\int X_\theta^*(B^*M_\theta B)X_\theta\,d\mu\succeq0.
 \end{aligned}}

\]

image. Multiplication by the literal $\chi$, followed by
the inherited finite tensor theta primitive, realizes
that field in the original cochain complex.

The relation to the particular mean-zero contraction is also exact.

\[
 \overline C=\int C_\theta\,d\mu,\quad
 a_C=C-\overline C:E\to B_N,\quad
 h_\theta=C_\theta-\overline C:E\to B_N.
 \tag{HCD14}
\]

the field $h_\theta$. The original discrepancy is
$C-C_\theta=a_C-h_\theta$ and need not have mean zero.
Since $a_C$ has relation-valued columns, phase and
common-source orthogonality give
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int a_C^*M_\theta h_\theta\,d\mu
 &=-a_C^*M\overline C\\
 &=-a_C^*M(C-a_C)=a_C^*Ma_C.
 \end{split}
 \tag{HCD15}
\]

 \boxed{\mathscr D
 =\int h_\theta^*M_\theta h_\theta\,d\mu-a_C^*Ma_C.}
 \tag{HCD16}
\]

not presumed orthogonal to constant relations for the
varying metric. At $N=q-1$, $B_N=0$,
$C_\theta=C=J^{-1}$, $a_C=h_\theta=0$ and $\overline G=G$.

and $c=k/2$. Retain
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 u_n(\theta)=(2\pi n+\theta)/L,\qquad
 s_n(\theta)=c+iu_n(\theta),\\
 w_n(\theta)=\frac{2\pi}{L}m_{h,k}(u_n(\theta))\ge0,
 \qquad n\in\mathbb Z.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{HCD17}
\]
The Fourier coefficient is literally $2\pi/L$, with
$m_{h,k}=w_h^{*k}$, $w_h=|(g/h)(1/2+iu)|^2/(2\pi)$
and $g=2\xi$. Sampling gives
\[
 \mathsf T_\theta P=(P(s_n(\theta)))_n,\qquad
 \|\mathsf T_\theta P\|_\theta^2
 =\sum_n w_n(\theta)|P(s_n(\theta))|^2=P^*M_\theta P.
 \tag{HCD18}
\]
This is the actual phase source Gram H17.

Define $\mathcal H_\theta$ to be weighted square-summable
sequences modulo sequences supported where $w_n(\theta)=0$.
Thus zero weights, possible when $k=1$, have an explicit
null subspace. For $k\ge2$, positivity of the original
convolution makes every sample weight positive.
At $k=1$, retain the exact ideal equality
$(\chi_{h,1})=(h)$. If $a_h\ne0$ is the original leading
coefficient of $h$, then $\chi_{h,1}=h/a_h$ is its monic
generator, and $\chi_{h,1}=h$ in the original monic packet
convention. Indeed a polynomial annihilates multiplication by

zero, which is equivalent to belonging to $(h)$.
The analytic source remains the original $g/h$, with
the factor $a_h$ retained in that quotient and its norm.
Now take a complete selected root
$\rho=1/2+iu_n(\theta)$ whose common order in $g$ and $h$
is $m$. The two Taylor expansions have leading coefficients
$g^{(m)}(\rho)/m!$ and $h^{(m)}(\rho)/m!$, so the canceled

\[
 (g/h)(\rho)=\frac{g^{(m)}(\rho)}{h^{(m)}(\rho)},\qquad
 w_n(\theta)=\frac1L
 \left|\frac{g^{(m)}(\rho)}{h^{(m)}(\rho)}\right|^2>0.
 \tag{HCD18a}
\]

map without changing a mass. The range projections are
measurable diagonal matrices; their images of the countable

\[
 A_\gamma=\|e^{\gamma|\cdot|}w_h\|_\infty,\qquad
 B_\gamma=\|e^{\gamma|\cdot|}w_h\|_1.
\]

its full degree, and the continuous canceled values on the
compact interval containing its selected roots. With

\[
 e^{\gamma|u|}m_{h,k}(u)
 \le f_\gamma^{*k}(u)
 \le A_\gamma B_\gamma^{k-1}.
 \tag{HCD19a}
\]

\[

 \tag{HCD19}

\[
 \frac{2\pi}{L}A_\gamma B_\gamma^{k-1}

 \left(1+\frac{2e^{-2\pi d/L}}{1-e^{-2\pi d/L}}\right).
\]
For every fixed polynomial $Q$, the constant
$\sup_{u\in\R}|Q(c+iu)|^2e^{-d|u|/2}$ is finite.
Inserting it into the same geometric estimate, with
$d/2$ in place of $d$, proves uniform exponential
summability of $w_n(\theta)|Q(s_n(\theta))|^2$.
This includes $Q=\chi$ and every fixed polynomial
relation used below. All original constants in the
weights are unchanged. The full source proof of
PSD8--PSD14 is a dependency of this continuation;

\section{Density and the complete fibrewise Hilbert quotient}

Here is a direct density proof with the zero weights retained.
If $f\in\mathcal H_\theta$ is orthogonal to all polynomials,
put $a_n=w_n(\theta)\overline{f_n}$. Cauchy--Schwarz and
(HCD19) give $\sum|a_n|e^{\epsilon|u_n|}<\infty$.
Hence $F(z)=\sum_n a_ne^{zu_n}$ is holomorphic on
$|\Re z|<\epsilon$, with termwise derivatives on smaller
closed strips. Every derivative at zero is zero, since
polynomials in $S$ and in $(S-c)/i$ span the same space.
The Taylor series and the identity theorem give $F=0$
on the connected strip. On the imaginary axis,
\[
 F(it)=e^{it\theta/L}\sum_n a_ne^{2\pi int/L}.
\]
The series is absolutely uniformly convergent.
Multiplication by $e^{-it\theta/L}e^{-2\pi imt/L}$ and
integration over $0\le t\le L$ give $a_m=0$.
At positive weights this implies $f_m=0$; at zero weights
the class is already null. Thus polynomials are dense.
The identical argument proves polynomial density for
the weights $w_n|\chi(s_n)|^2$.

Multiplication by the original polynomial is the isometry
\[
 U_\chi:\ell^2(w_n|\chi(s_n)|^2)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_\theta,
 \qquad f\longmapsto(\chi(s_n)f_n)_n.
 \tag{HCD20}
\]
Its image is precisely the sequences vanishing at the
positive-weight sampled roots of $\chi$. To prove the
converse inclusion, take such a sequence $v$ and set
$f_n=v_n/\chi(s_n)$ when $\chi(s_n)\ne0$, and zero
elsewhere. Its squared domain norm equals $\|v\|_\theta^2$.
Thus the image is closed. Polynomial density in the domain
now proves
\[
 \mathcal R_\theta:=
 \overline{\chi\C[S]}^{\,\mathcal H_\theta}
 =\{v:v_n=0\text{ if }w_n(\theta)>0,\ \chi(s_n(\theta))=0\}.
 \tag{HCD21}
\]
The receiving Hilbert quotient is exactly
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathcal Q_\theta=\mathcal H_\theta/\mathcal R_\theta
 \simeq
 \bigoplus_{\substack{n:\chi(s_n(\theta))=0\\w_n(\theta)>0}}\C,\\
 \|v\|_{\mathcal Q_\theta}^2
 =\sum_{\rm displayed\ n}w_n(\theta)|v_n|^2.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{HCD22}
\]
The quotient map is orthogonal coordinate restriction.
No weight equal to zero is inverted.

\section{The complete primary kernel before phase integration}

Let $\Lambda_\theta^+$ be the distinct sampled roots of
$\chi$ with positive weight, and set
$p_\theta(S)=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\theta^+}(S-\lambda)$,
using $p_\theta=1$ for an empty product.
The finite map is
\[
 \rho_\theta:E\longrightarrow\mathcal Q_\theta,\qquad
 [P]_\chi\longmapsto(P(\lambda))_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\theta^+}.
 \tag{HCD23}
\]
It is well defined, and is onto by Lagrange interpolation
at these distinct points, using degree less than
$|\Lambda_\theta^+|\le q$. Vanishing at all those points
is equivalent to divisibility by $p_\theta$. Since
$p_\theta\mid\chi$,
\[
 \ker\rho_\theta=(p_\theta)/(\chi)\subset E.
 \tag{HCD24}
\]
This specifies the zero-weight-corrected kernel in H64:
a root at a zero-mass coordinate contributes no receiving
Hilbert line.

Write the full original factorization as
$\chi=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(S-\lambda)^{m_\lambda}$.
The complete Taylor map is
\[
 \begin{split}
 E&\longrightarrow\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
 \C[\varepsilon_\lambda]/(\varepsilon_\lambda^{m_\lambda}),\\
 [P]&\longmapsto\left(

\[
 U_\chi:\ell^2(w_n|\chi(s_n)|^2)\longrightarrow\mathcal H_\theta,
 \qquad f\longmapsto(\chi(s_n)f_n)_n.
 \tag{HCD20}
\]
Its image is precisely the sequences vanishing at the
positive-weight sampled roots of $\chi$. To prove the
converse inclusion, take such a sequence $v$ and set
$f_n=v_n/\chi(s_n)$ when $\chi(s_n)\ne0$, and zero
elsewhere. Its squared domain norm equals $\|v\|_\theta^2$.
Thus the image is closed. Polynomial density in the domain
now proves
\[
 \mathcal R_\theta:=
 \overline{\chi\C[S]}^{\,\mathcal H_\theta}
 =\{v:v_n=0\text{ if }w_n(\theta)>0,\ \chi(s_n(\theta))=0\}.
 \tag{HCD21}
\]
The receiving Hilbert quotient is exactly
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathcal Q_\theta=\mathcal H_\theta/\mathcal R_\theta
 \simeq
 \bigoplus_{\substack{n:\chi(s_n(\theta))=0\\w_n(\theta)>0}}\C,\\
 \|v\|_{\mathcal Q_\theta}^2
 =\sum_{\rm displayed\ n}w_n(\theta)|v_n|^2.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{HCD22}
\]
The quotient map is orthogonal coordinate restriction.
No weight equal to zero is inverted.

\section{The complete primary kernel before phase integration}

Let $\Lambda_\theta^+$ be the distinct sampled roots of
$\chi$ with positive weight, and set
$p_\theta(S)=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\theta^+}(S-\lambda)$,
using $p_\theta=1$ for an empty product.
The finite map is
\[
 \rho_\theta:E\longrightarrow\mathcal Q_\theta,\qquad
 [P]_\chi\longmapsto(P(\lambda))_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\theta^+}.
 \tag{HCD23}
\]
It is well defined, and is onto by Lagrange interpolation
at these distinct points, using degree less than
$|\Lambda_\theta^+|\le q$. Vanishing at all those points
is equivalent to divisibility by $p_\theta$. Since
$p_\theta\mid\chi$,
\[
 \ker\rho_\theta=(p_\theta)/(\chi)\subset E.
 \tag{HCD24}
\]
This specifies the zero-weight-corrected kernel in H64:
a root at a zero-mass coordinate contributes no receiving
Hilbert line.

Write the full original factorization as
$\chi=\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(S-\lambda)^{m_\lambda}$.
The complete Taylor map is
\[
 \begin{split}
 E&\longrightarrow\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
 \C[\varepsilon_\lambda]/(\varepsilon_\lambda^{m_\lambda}),\\
 [P]&\longmapsto\left(
 \sum_{j=0}^{m_\lambda-1}\frac{P^{(j)}(\lambda)}{j!}
 \varepsilon_\lambda^j\right)_\lambda.
 \end{split}
 \tag{HCD25}
\]
For an explicit inverse, let
$q_\lambda=\chi/(S-\lambda)^{m_\lambda}$ and let
$u_\lambda$ be the Taylor polynomial of $1/q_\lambda$
at $\lambda$ through degree $m_\lambda-1$.
Then $e_\lambda=[u_\lambda q_\lambda]_\chi$ is one
in the $\lambda$ factor and zero in every other factor,
by divisibility by each original prime power. It follows
that $\sum e_\lambda=1$ and the factors are orthogonal
idempotents. The inverse is
$\sum_\lambda e_\lambda\sum_j a_{\lambda,j}(S-\lambda)^j$.

In these full primary coordinates, $\rho_\theta$ takes
the constant coefficient of each active sampled factor.
Its kernel in that factor is $(\varepsilon_\lambda)$,
retaining every order $1,\ldots,m_\lambda-1$.
For an unsampled factor or a zero-weight sampled factor,
the kernel is the entire primary algebra, including
its constant term. The original action is multiplication
by $\lambda+\varepsilon_\lambda$; the receiving action
is the simple scalar $\lambda$. Evaluation intertwines
these actions with the displayed nilpotent kernel.

\section{The measurable completed field and its vanishing map}

Every sampled root has real part $c$. For a fixed root $\lambda$
with $\Re\lambda=c$, its only possible phase is
\[
 \theta_\lambda=L\Im\lambda\pmod{2\pi},\quad
 0\le\theta_\lambda<2\pi,\qquad
 n_\lambda=(L\Im\lambda-\theta_\lambda)/(2\pi)\in\mathbb Z.
\]
Thus the set $\Theta_\chi$ of possible phases is finite.
For $\theta\notin\Theta_\chi$, $\mathcal Q_\theta=0$.
At an exceptional phase the positive-weight condition
in (HCD22) is still retained.

In the measurable realization after (HCD18), the projection
onto $\mathcal Q_\theta$ has diagonal entries
\[
 {\bf1}_{\{w_n(\theta)>0\}}
 {\bf1}_{\{\chi(s_n(\theta))=0\}},\qquad n\in\mathbb Z.
\]
These are measurable and give an explicit field of projections.
The direct integral satisfies
\[
 \mathscr Q=\int_\Theta^\oplus\mathcal Q_\theta\,d\mu=0,
 \tag{HCD26}
\]
because every measurable section has squared norm supported
on the finite measure-zero set $\Theta_\chi$.
This is an almost-everywhere assertion; each exceptional
nonzero receiving line is still exactly the weighted line
in (HCD22).

For $x\in E$, the section $\theta\mapsto\rho_\theta x$
is measurable: it is given by polynomial evaluations and
the displayed coordinate masks. It defines
\[
 \rho:E\longrightarrow\mathscr Q,\qquad
 x\longmapsto[\theta\mapsto\rho_\theta x]_{\rm a.e.},
 \qquad \ker\rho=E.
 \tag{HCD27}
\]
Every pointwise exceptional value has zero direct-integral
class. This does not assert that those pointwise maps vanish,
or that the original nonreduced coefficient algebra was zero.

\section{The source-to-completion cochain map}

The direct-integral source is the weighted space with squared
norm $\int_\Theta\sum_n w_n(\theta)|v_n(\theta)|^2\,d\mu$.
Let $\mathscr H$ denote this space, and let $\mathscr R$
be its closed subspace of sections belonging to
$\mathcal R_\theta$ almost everywhere. The coordinate
projection above has kernel $\mathscr R$.

The measurable evaluation map is
\[
 \mathsf T:\mathscr P\longrightarrow\mathscr H,\qquad
 P\longmapsto(P(\theta,s_n(\theta)))_{\theta,n}.
\]
The integrated identity (HCD18) proves it is an isometry.
Evaluation of a relation-valued section is in $\mathscr R$,
because the original section is a multiple of the literal
$\chi$. Hence there is a cochain map
\[
 [\mathscr B\hookrightarrow\mathscr P^{\rm eq}]
 \longrightarrow[\mathscr R\hookrightarrow\mathscr H],
 \tag{HCD28}
\]
using evaluation in both degrees. On a common image $x$,
the receiving quotient value is $\rho_\theta x$, since
representatives differ by an original relation.
The induced degree-one map is exactly (HCD27).

The global relation subspace is also the closure of measurable
finite polynomial relation sections. To prove this without
a measurable choice of approximating polynomials, suppose
$v\in\mathscr H$ is orthogonal to every section
$\mathbf1_U(\theta)\chi(S)S^j$, for measurable $U$ and $j\ge0$.
Its fibre inner product with $\chi S^j$ is integrable by
Cauchy--Schwarz, and its integral over every $U$ is zero,
so that inner product is zero almost everywhere.
The original exponential sample bounds make every fixed
polynomial section square-integrable.
Intersecting the countably many resulting full-measure sets,
(HCD21) gives $v(\theta)\in\mathcal Q_\theta$ there.
Conversely every such section is orthogonal to the relations.
The orthogonal-complement characterization proves that their
closed span is exactly $\mathscr R$.

Since $\mathscr Q=0$, $\mathscr R=\mathscr H$ as Hilbert
spaces, and the completed complex is the identity complex.
Its degree-one cohomology is zero. The finite continuous
common-image complex has positive Gram $\overline G$
on its full $E$ by (HCD8)--(HCD12).
The intervening map and its whole kernel are precisely
(HCD23)--(HCD28).

\section{The receiving supported zero and all marked fibres}

Integrate in the stated coefficient fibre, then apply the
original marked support construction. At a fixed original
label $\ell$, a linear map $f$ has the lift
\[
 (\ell,x)\longmapsto(\ell,f(x)),\qquad
 \tau\longmapsto\tau.
 \tag{HCD29}
\]
For (HCD27), every represented input maps to the receiving
supported zero $(\ell,0)$, and external absence maps to
external absence $\tau$. Their inverse images are respectively
the full represented fibre and the singleton external absence.
At a fixed phase, the represented kernel is the entire
ideal (HCD24), with its full primary decomposition (HCD25).
No integral on arbitrary mixed-support totals is presumed.

If the empty-packet case $q=0$ is separately admitted,
$E=0$, $B_N=P_N$, and the finite and continuous coefficient
complexes are identity complexes. The quotient Gram
determinant is the empty determinant one. The analytic
source and its literal norm remain present before the
quotient. Its marked receiving object still has $\tau$
and the represented zero, with the same maps (HCD29).

\section{Exact outcome and scope}

The continuous common-image complex has the explicit bounded
cochain contraction (HCD7) on its complement and retains
the whole nonreduced quotient in degree one.
Its minimum metric is $\overline G$, and its difference
from the constant-source metric is the positive original
relation norm (HCD13). The mean-zero decomposition retains
the weighted cross term (HCD15), giving (HCD16).

The subsequent completion has receiving weighted value
spaces (HCD22), primary kernels (HCD24)--(HCD25), measurable
field (HCD26), and actual cochain map (HCD28).
Its receiving coefficient direct integral is zero because
only finitely many phases can sample a fixed polynomial root.
Every exceptional phase, nilpotent component and zero-weight
coordinate remains in the stated maps and kernels.
No arithmetic volume asymptotic or RH conclusion is inferred.
